# scRNAseq and snRNAseq pre-processing
This is the pre-processing and annotation of the sc/snRNA-seq data from:
"Chen, M. M., Gao, Q., Ning, H., Chen, K., Gao, Y., Yu, M., ... & Zhang, Z. (2025). Integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomics uncover distinct cellular subtypes involved in neural invasion in pancreatic cancer. Cancer Cell."

The annotated data will be used to deconvolve the ST data that we have.

#===================================================================
# WHAT THIS SCRIPT PRODUCES
#===================================================================
# Handoff (input/):
#   - sc_sn_merged_obj.Rds
#       *** THE FILE. Saved to input/, not output/, since every other
#       script in this project that references the Chen et al. sc/snRNA
#       reference (celltype specificity, DRAXIN analysis) treats it as
#       a fixed input -- same convention as Integrated_NMF.rds and
#       DE_SPE_annotaion.csv. ***
#
# Figures (output/00_scRNA_snRNA_preprocessing/figures/):
#   - scRNA_QC_violin.pdf / snRNA_QC_violin.pdf
#       nFeature_RNA / nCount_RNA / percent.mt violin plots supporting
#       the QC filtering thresholds used below (not saved in the
#       original script -- added here so the QC rationale has a
#       persistent record).
#
# SCOPING NOTE (raised during review, kept as-is by design -- documented
# here for transparency rather than changed): this script's merged
# reference INCLUDES BOTH PNI-High and PNI-Low patients -- i.e. the RCTD
# deconvolution reference is built from the fullest, most representative
# pool of reference cells available. This is a deliberate, different
# scoping decision from later analyses (e.g. the DRAXIN cell-type-
# specificity script), which restrict to PNI-High only for reasons
# specific to that analysis (matching this project's own high-PNI
# disease context; PNI-Low Schwann cells there showed a severe single-
# patient bias). Building the deconvolution REFERENCE from the full
# cohort and restricting DOWNSTREAM INTERPRETATION to a clinically
# matched subset are two different, independently justifiable choices --
# noted explicitly here so the difference in scope between this script
# and later ones is not mistaken for an inconsistency.
#
# REPRODUCIBILITY NOTE: added set.seed() before the stochastic steps
# (RunPCA, RunBBKNN, FindClusters) that were previously unseeded. This
# does not affect the critical cell_type_refined assignments below,
# which come directly from the authors' own provided metadata (barcode
# mapping), not from this script's own clustering -- but the PCA/BBKNN/
# UMAP embedding and cluster labels themselves were previously not
# guaranteed reproducible run-to-run.
#===================================================================

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(readxl)

# ---- 0. Directory structure -------------------------------------------
PROJECT_ROOT  <- "/media/Aleksandra/Computational/R programming/Publication_files/publication_cleaned"
PROJECT_DIR   <- PROJECT_ROOT
INPUT_DIR     <- file.path(PROJECT_DIR, "input")

ANALYSIS_NAME <- "04_scRNA_snRNA_preprocessing"
FIGURES_DIR   <- file.path(PROJECT_DIR, "output", ANALYSIS_NAME, "figures")
dir.create(INPUT_DIR,   recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(FIGURES_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

set.seed(42)

# NOTE: place the GEO-downloaded 10X directories and metadata.csv files
# into paper_revision_codes/input/GEOdata/scRNAseq/ and
# paper_revision_codes/input/GEOdata/snRNAseq/ before running.
scRNA.data <- Read10X(data.dir = file.path(INPUT_DIR, "GEOdata", "scRNAseq"))
# Initialize the Seurat object with the raw (non-normalized data).
scRNA <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = scRNA.data, project = "scRNA", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)

snRNA.data <- Read10X(data.dir = file.path(INPUT_DIR, "GEOdata", "snRNAseq"))
# Initialize the Seurat object with the raw (non-normalized data).
snRNA <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = snRNA.data, project = "snRNA", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)

```

```{r}
scRNA[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(scRNA, pattern = "^MT-")
p_qc_sc <- VlnPlot(scRNA, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), ncol = 3)
p_qc_sc
ggsave(file.path(FIGURES_DIR, "scRNA_QC_violin.pdf"), p_qc_sc, width = 12, height = 5)
```
```{r}
snRNA[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(snRNA, pattern = "^MT-")
p_qc_sn <- VlnPlot(snRNA, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), ncol = 3)
p_qc_sn
ggsave(file.path(FIGURES_DIR, "snRNA_QC_violin.pdf"), p_qc_sn, width = 12, height = 5)
```
```{r}
scRNA <- subset(scRNA, subset = nFeature_RNA > 200 & nFeature_RNA < 6000 & percent.mt < 25 & nCount_RNA < 25000)

snRNA <- subset(snRNA, subset = nFeature_RNA > 200 & nFeature_RNA < 6000 & percent.mt < 25 & nCount_RNA < 25000)
```

Now we want to map the metadata provided by the authors in our Seurat object
```{r}
scRNA_metadata <- read.csv(file.path(INPUT_DIR, "GEOdata", "scRNAseq", "metadata.csv"))
scRNA$barcode <-names(scRNA@active.ident)
scRNA$cell_type <- plyr::mapvalues(scRNA$barcode, from = scRNA_metadata$X, to=scRNA_metadata$all_celltype)
scRNA <- subset(scRNA, subset = !is.na(cell_type))
scRNA$tissue <- plyr::mapvalues(scRNA$barcode, from = scRNA_metadata$X, to=scRNA_metadata$tissue)
scRNA$patients <- plyr::mapvalues(scRNA$barcode, from = scRNA_metadata$X, to=scRNA_metadata$patients)
```

```{r}
snRNA_metadata <- read.csv(file.path(INPUT_DIR, "GEOdata", "snRNAseq", "metadata.csv"))
snRNA$barcode <-names(snRNA@active.ident)
snRNA$cell_type <- plyr::mapvalues(snRNA$barcode, from = snRNA_metadata$X, to=snRNA_metadata$all_celltype)
snRNA <- subset(snRNA, subset = !is.na(cell_type))
snRNA$tissue <- plyr::mapvalues(snRNA$barcode, from = snRNA_metadata$X, to=snRNA_metadata$tissue)
snRNA$patients <- plyr::mapvalues(snRNA$barcode, from = snRNA_metadata$X, to=snRNA_metadata$patients)
```

```{r}
merged_obj <- merge(x = scRNA, y = snRNA, add.cell.ids = c("scRNA", "snRNA"),)
# For our analysis we don't need the PBMC data so we remove them
merged_obj <- subset(merged_obj, subset = !(merged_obj$tissue == "PBMC"))
# SCOPING NOTE (see header): tissue is NOT further restricted by PNI
# status here -- both PNI-High and PNI-Low patients remain in this
# reference. This is intentional; see header for rationale.
merged_obj <- NormalizeData(merged_obj)
merged_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(merged_obj)
merged_obj <- ScaleData(merged_obj)
merged_obj <- RunPCA(merged_obj)
```
Then, according to the authors, we integrated the two datasets with the following parameters and function:
```{r}
#devtools::install_github("ycli1995/bbknnR")
library(bbknnR)
merged_obj <- RunBBKNN(merged_obj, batch_key = 'orig.ident', n_pcs = 30,run_UMAP = TRUE)
```
```{r}
merged_obj <- FindNeighbors(merged_obj, dims = 1:10)
merged_obj <- FindClusters(merged_obj, resolution = 1)
```

```{r}
merged_obj <- JoinLayers(merged_obj)
DimPlot(merged_obj, reduction = "umap")
```
We can use their metadata to characterize the ductal malignant cells as follows:
```{r}
# make a character copy so new labels are allowed
merged_obj$cell_type_refined <- as.character(merged_obj$cell_type)

merged_obj$cell_type_refined[merged_obj$cell_type == "Ductal" & merged_obj$tissue == "Tumor"]           <- "Ductal_malignant"
merged_obj$cell_type_refined[merged_obj$cell_type == "Ductal" & merged_obj$tissue == "Adjacent_normal"] <- "Ductal_normal"
merged_obj <- subset(merged_obj, subset = !(merged_obj$cell_type_refined == "Platelet")) # Because after removing PBMC samples only 2 cells left and that leads to errors when running RCTD
```
Now we can use this for the reference.
```{r}
saveRDS(merged_obj, file.path(INPUT_DIR, "sc_sn_merged_obj.Rds"))
cat("Saved:", file.path(INPUT_DIR, "sc_sn_merged_obj.Rds"), "\n")
cat("This file is now the primary sc/snRNA-seq reference for every\n")
cat("downstream script in this project that uses it (celltype\n")
cat("specificity, DRAXIN Chen-reference analysis).\n")
```
